## Comparability caveat (important)

These two fiscal years are **not directly comparable on an as-reported basis**. GE spun off GE HealthCare on January 3, 2023 and GE Vernova on April 2, 2024; both are reported as **discontinued operations for all periods presented** in the FY2024 filing, and the continuing-operations entity is what is now called GE Aerospace [ge_fy2024_notes.txt]. So the FY2022 figure in the original FY2022 10-K ($76,555M, the whole conglomerate) [ge_fy2022_10k.txt] and the FY2023 10-K's restated FY2022 ($58,100M, ex-HealthCare only) [ge_fy2023_10k.txt] both reflect a materially larger business than today's GE Aerospace.

The only apples-to-apples comparison is the **recast, continuing-operations (GE Aerospace) basis** used in the FY2024 10-K.

## Calculation (like-for-like, GE Aerospace continuing operations)

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| FY2022 total revenue (recast in FY2024 10-K) | $29,139M [ge_fy2024_income_statement.txt] |
| FY2024 total revenue | $38,702M [ge_fy2024_income_statement.txt] |
| Growth | +$9,563M, **+32.8%** |
| Implied CAGR (2 yrs) | ~15.2% |

For contrast, naively comparing FY2024 GE Aerospace revenue to the originally reported FY2022 GE total of $76,555M would show a ~49% *decline*, and versus the FY2023 10-K's $58,100M a ~33% decline — but those differences reflect the HealthCare and Vernova separations, not underlying business performance.

ANSWER: On a like-for-like continuing-operations (GE Aerospace) basis, revenue grew ~32.8%, from $29,139M in FY2022 (as recast) to $38,702M in FY2024 (+$9,563M; ~15.2% CAGR). Note this is not comparable to GE's originally reported FY2022 revenue of $76,555M, which included the since-separated HealthCare and Vernova businesses.
